cohort: 103 women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss and 204 pregnant women with low-risk pregnancies (control group)
finding: Women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss had a high reproductive success rate (91.2%), suggesting that with appropriate healthcare services, such as prenatal care, cervical cerclage, and hospital care, good outcomes are achievable.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was more common in the loss group (64.7%) compared to the control group (39.5%).
